summary: The bill bars the Department of Homeland Security from entering contracts, using funds, or taking other actions to build, expand, or operate any new immigration detention facilities in warehouses, tents, modular units, or similar non-traditional structures.

scores.thoughts: The bill explicitly prohibits DHS/ICE from obligating or expending funds to establish, construct, renovate, expand, or operate new immigration detention models (warehouses, tents, modular facilities, etc.). It further requires that any such obligated amounts be transferred to other services. This directly restricts federal spending in a specific area, pushing toward reduced government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue collection.
The bill redirects certain funds to 'affordable health care,' but this is a minor, incidental provision rather than a substantive change to healthcare policy or structure.
No provisions address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The core purpose of the bill is to block DHS from creating or expanding any new immigration detention capacity (including non-traditional facilities). This directly limits immigration enforcement tools and expands protections for immigrants by preventing additional detention, aligning strongly with the -1 pole.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill addresses DHS/ICE civil immigration detention, not Department of Defense or military spending.
Findings mention environmental impacts of detention facilities, but the bill does not enact any environmental regulations or policy changes.
The bill redirects funds from new detention to 'affordable health care and housing,' which constitutes a modest expansion of safety-net-type services.
No provisions address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related policies.
The bill concerns civil immigration detention rather than criminal sentencing, policing, or justice reform.
No provisions address trade, tariffs, or globalization.
By prohibiting new detention spending and redirecting funds, the bill modestly reduces federal outlays, which leans toward debt reduction, though the effect is narrow.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No provisions address foreign aid or international assistance.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance policy.
No provisions address unions, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
